facts.definition: A graph of entities connected by typed relationships that represents facts about a domain.
A real-world thing, such as a person, place or course, represented as a node in a knowledge graph.
A single fact written as subject, predicate and object.
The set of types and relationship kinds that the data in a knowledge graph uses.
A W3C data model that describes resources as subject-predicate-object triples.
A global identifier that RDF uses to name resources and properties.
A value such as a string, number or date that can be the object of an RDF triple.
A compact text syntax for writing RDF graphs.
A resource in an RDF graph that has no global identifier.
The W3C query language for RDF data.
A SPARQL query form that returns a table of variable bindings.
A triple in which the subject, predicate or object can be a variable.
A SPARQL clause that keeps only the solutions for which a condition is true.
A SPARQL clause that adds matches when they exist but keeps the solution when they do not.
The W3C Web Ontology Language for describing classes, properties and their logical relationships.
A set of individuals that share characteristics, such as all students.
A specific member of a class, such as one particular student.
A property that links one individual to another individual.
A property that links an individual to a literal value.
Software that perceives its environment and acts on its own to reach goals.
A system in which several agents interact to solve a problem that is hard for one agent alone.
A component that coordinates other agents and combines their results.
A design in which a person reviews or approves actions before they take effect.
An upper bound on how the running time or memory of an algorithm grows with the input size.
Running time that grows in direct proportion to the input size, O(n).
Running time that grows with the logarithm of the input size, O(log n), as in binary search.
Running time that grows with the square of the input size, O(n^2).
A divide-and-conquer sort that splits the list, sorts each half and merges them in O(n log n) time.
A divide-and-conquer sort that partitions around a pivot; O(n log n) on average and O(n^2) in the worst case.
A sort that builds the result one element at a time and is fast for small or nearly sorted lists.
A sort that keeps equal elements in their original relative order.
An in-place sort that uses a binary heap and runs in O(n log n) time in the worst case.
A graph traversal that visits all neighbours of a node before it goes deeper; it finds shortest paths in unweighted graphs.
A graph traversal that follows one path as deep as possible before it backtracks.
A shortest-path algorithm for graphs with non-negative edge weights.
A graph representation that stores, for each node, the list of its neighbours.
A method that solves a problem from the solutions of overlapping subproblems and stores them to avoid repeated work.
Storing the results of function calls so that the same call is not computed again.
A property where an optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions of its subproblems.
A bottom-up dynamic programming style that fills a table from the smallest subproblems up.
